audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for miraculous catch, calling Simon/James/John, cleansing of skin disease, paralyzed man, Levi call, table fellowship, fasting, and new wine/wineskins.

verses.restored: It happened as the crowd pressed upon him to hear the word of the Divine, he was standing beside the lake of Gennesaret.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that, as the people pressed upon him to hear the word of God, he stood by the lake of Gennesaret,

modern.text: On one occasion, while Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret with the crowd pressing in on Him to hear the word of God,

original.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ τὸν ὄχλον ἐπικεῖσθαι αὐτῷ ⸀καὶ ἀκούειν τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἑστὼς παρὰ τὴν λίμνην Γεννησαρέτ,

verses.restored: He saw two boats standing beside the lake; the fishers had gone out from them and were washing the nets.

familiar.text: And saw two ships standing by the lake: but the fishermen were gone out of them, and were washing their nets.

modern.text: He saw two boats at the edge of the lake. The fishermen had left them and were washing their nets.

original.text: καὶ εἶδεν ⸂δύο πλοῖα⸃ ἑστῶτα παρὰ τὴν λίμνην, οἱ δὲ ἁλιεῖς ⸂ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ἀποβάντες⸃ ⸀ἔπλυνον τὰ δίκτυα.

verses.restored: Entering one of the boats, which was Simon's, he asked him to put out a little from the land; sitting down, he taught the crowds from the boat.

familiar.text: And he entered into one of the ships, which was Simon’s, and prayed him that he would thrust out a little from the land. And he sat down, and taught the people out of the ship.

modern.text: Jesus got into the boat belonging to Simon and asked him to put out a little from shore. And sitting down, He taught the people from the boat.

original.text: ἐμβὰς δὲ εἰς ἓν τῶν πλοίων, ὃ ⸀ἦν Σίμωνος, ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἐπαναγαγεῖν ὀλίγον, ⸂καθίσας δὲ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου ἐδίδασκεν⸃ τοὺς ὄχλους.

verses.restored: When he stopped speaking, he said to Simon, Put out into the deep and let down your nets for a catch.

familiar.text: Now when he had left speaking, he said unto Simon, Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.

modern.text: When Jesus had finished speaking, He said to Simon, “Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch.”

original.text: ὡς δὲ ἐπαύσατο λαλῶν, εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα· Ἐπανάγαγε εἰς τὸ βάθος καὶ χαλάσατε τὰ δίκτυα ὑμῶν εἰς ἄγραν.

verses.restored: Simon answered, Master, through the whole night we labored and took nothing; but at your word I will let down the nets.

familiar.text: And Simon answering said unto him, Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net.

modern.text: “Master,” Simon replied, “we have worked hard all night without catching anything. But because You say so, I will let down the nets.”

original.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ⸀Σίμων ⸀εἶπεν· Ἐπιστάτα, διʼ ⸀ὅλης νυκτὸς κοπιάσαντες οὐδὲν ἐλάβομεν, ἐπὶ δὲ τῷ ῥήματί σου χαλάσω ⸂τὰ δίκτυα⸃.

verses.restored: Doing this, they enclosed a great multitude of fish, and their nets were breaking.

familiar.text: And when they had this done, they inclosed a great multitude of fishes: and their net brake.

modern.text: When they had done so, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear.

original.text: καὶ τοῦτο ποιήσαντες συνέκλεισαν πλῆθος ἰχθύων πολύ, ⸀διερρήσσετο δὲ ⸂τὰ δίκτυα⸃ αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: They signaled to partners in the other boat to come help them; they came and filled both boats, so that they were sinking.

familiar.text: And they beckoned unto their partners, which were in the other ship, that they should come and help them. And they came, and filled both the ships, so that they began to sink.

modern.text: So they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them, and they came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink.

original.text: καὶ κατένευσαν τοῖς ⸀μετόχοις ἐν τῷ ἑτέρῳ πλοίῳ τοῦ ἐλθόντας συλλαβέσθαι αὐτοῖς· καὶ ἦλθον, καὶ ἔπλησαν ἀμφότερα τὰ πλοῖα ὥστε βυθίζεσθαι αὐτά.

verses.restored: Seeing this, Simon Peter fell at Jesus' knees, saying, Depart from me, Lord, because I am a sinful/misaligned man.

familiar.text: When Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.

modern.text: When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees. “Go away from me, Lord,” he said, “for I am a sinful man.”

original.text: ἰδὼν δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος προσέπεσεν τοῖς γόνασιν Ἰησοῦ λέγων· Ἔξελθε ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ, ὅτι ἀνὴρ ἁμαρτωλός εἰμι, κύριε·

verses.restored: For astonishment seized him and all those with him at the catch of fish they had taken.

familiar.text: For he was astonished, and all that were with him, at the draught of the fishes which they had taken:

modern.text: For he and his companions were astonished at the catch of fish they had taken,

original.text: θάμβος γὰρ περιέσχεν αὐτὸν καὶ πάντας τοὺς σὺν αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τῇ ἄγρᾳ τῶν ἰχθύων ⸀ὧν συνέλαβον,

verses.restored: Likewise also James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. Jesus said to Simon, Do not fear; from now you will be catching people alive.

familiar.text: And so was also James, and John, the sons of Zebedee, which were partners with Simon. And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.

modern.text: and so were his partners James and John, the sons of Zebedee. “Do not be afraid,” Jesus said to Simon. “From now on you will catch men.”

original.text: ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην υἱοὺς Ζεβεδαίου, οἳ ἦσαν κοινωνοὶ τῷ Σίμωνι. καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ φοβοῦ· ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ἀνθρώπους ἔσῃ ζωγρῶν.

verses.restored: Bringing the boats to land, leaving everything, they followed him.

familiar.text: And when they had brought their ships to land, they forsook all, and followed him.

modern.text: And when they had brought their boats ashore, they left everything and followed Him. The Leper’s Prayer (Leviticus 14:1–32; Matthew 8:1–4; Mark 1:40–45)

original.text: καὶ καταγαγόντες τὰ πλοῖα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἀφέντες ⸀πάντα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: While he was in one of the cities, look, a man full of skin disease. Seeing Jesus, he fell on his face and pleaded, Lord, if you are willing, you are able to cleanse me.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when he was in a certain city, behold a man full of leprosy: who seeing Jesus fell on his face, and besought him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.

modern.text: While Jesus was in one of the towns, a man came along who was covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell facedown and begged Him, “Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.”

original.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν μιᾷ τῶν πόλεων καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ πλήρης λέπρας· ⸂καὶ ἰδὼν⸃ τὸν Ἰησοῦν πεσὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον ἐδεήθη αὐτοῦ λέγων· Κύριε, ἐὰν θέλῃς δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι.

verses.restored: Stretching out his hand, he touched him, saying, I am willing; be cleansed. Immediately the skin disease left him.

familiar.text: And he put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will: be thou clean. And immediately the leprosy departed from him.

modern.text: Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” He said. “Be clean!” And immediately the leprosy left him.

original.text: καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἥψατο αὐτοῦ ⸀εἰπών· Θέλω, καθαρίσθητι· καὶ εὐθέως ἡ λέπρα ἀπῆλθεν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: He instructed him to tell no one, but, Go show yourself to the priest and offer for your cleansing as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.

familiar.text: And he charged him to tell no man: but go, and shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing, according as Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.

modern.text: “Do not tell anyone,” Jesus instructed him. “But go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.”

original.text: καὶ αὐτὸς παρήγγειλεν αὐτῷ μηδενὶ εἰπεῖν, ἀλλὰ ἀπελθὼν δεῖξον σεαυτὸν τῷ ἱερεῖ, καὶ προσένεγκε περὶ τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ σου καθὼς προσέταξεν Μωϋσῆς εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.

verses.restored: The word about him spread even more, and great crowds came together to hear and to be healed from their weaknesses.

familiar.text: But so much the more went there a fame abroad of him: and great multitudes came together to hear, and to be healed by him of their infirmities.

modern.text: But the news about Jesus spread all the more, and great crowds came to hear Him and to be healed of their sicknesses.

original.text: διήρχετο δὲ μᾶλλον ὁ λόγος περὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ συνήρχοντο ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἀκούειν καὶ ⸀θεραπεύεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἀσθενειῶν αὐτῶν·

verses.restored: But he would withdraw in deserted places and pray.

familiar.text: And he withdrew himself into the wilderness, and prayed.

modern.text: Yet He frequently withdrew to the wilderness to pray. Jesus Heals a Paralytic (Matthew 9:1–8; Mark 2:1–12)

original.text: αὐτὸς δὲ ἦν ὑποχωρῶν ἐν ταῖς ἐρήμοις καὶ προσευχόμενος.

verses.restored: On one of the days he was teaching, Pharisees and teachers of the Law were sitting there, who had come from every village of Galilee and Judea and from Jerusalem; and power of the Lord was with him to heal.

familiar.text: And it came to pass on a certain day, as he was teaching, that there were Pharisees and doctors of the law sitting by, which were come out of every town of Galilee, and Judaea, and Jerusalem: and the power of the Lord was present to heal them.

modern.text: One day Jesus was teaching, and the Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. People had come from Jerusalem and from every village of Galilee and Judea, and the power of the Lord was present for Him to heal the sick.

original.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν διδάσκων, καὶ ἦσαν καθήμενοι Φαρισαῖοι καὶ νομοδιδάσκαλοι οἳ ἦσαν ἐληλυθότες ἐκ πάσης κώμης τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλήμ· καὶ δύναμις κυρίου ἦν εἰς τὸ ἰᾶσθαι ⸀αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Look, men were carrying on a bed a person who was paralyzed, and they were seeking to bring him in and place him before Jesus.

familiar.text: And, behold, men brought in a bed a man which was taken with a palsy: and they sought means to bring him in, and to lay him before him.

modern.text: Just then some men came carrying a paralyzed man on a mat. They tried to bring him inside to set him before Jesus,

original.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες φέροντες ἐπὶ κλίνης ἄνθρωπον ὃς ἦν παραλελυμένος, καὶ ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν εἰσενεγκεῖν καὶ ⸀θεῖναι ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Not finding how to bring him in because of the crowd, they went up on the roof and lowered him through the tiles with the bed into the middle before Jesus.

familiar.text: And when they could not find by what way they might bring him in because of the multitude, they went upon the housetop, and let him down through the tiling with his couch into the midst before Jesus.

modern.text: but they could not find a way through the crowd. So they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles into the middle of the crowd, right in front of Jesus.

original.text: καὶ μὴ εὑρόντες ποίας εἰσενέγκωσιν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἀναβάντες ἐπὶ τὸ δῶμα διὰ τῶν κεράμων καθῆκαν αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ κλινιδίῳ εἰς τὸ μέσον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.

verses.restored: Seeing their trust, he said, Human one, your sins/misalignments are released for you.

familiar.text: And when he saw their faith, he said unto him, Man, thy sins are forgiven thee.

modern.text: When Jesus saw their faith, He said, “Friend, your sins are forgiven.”

original.text: καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν ⸀εἶπεν· Ἄνθρωπε, ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου.

verses.restored: The scribes and Pharisees began reasoning, saying, Who is this who speaks blasphemies? Who is able to release sins/misalignments except the Divine alone?

familiar.text: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, Who is this which speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?

modern.text: But the scribes and Pharisees began thinking to themselves, “Who is this man who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”

original.text: καὶ ἤρξαντο διαλογίζεσθαι οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι λέγοντες· Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος ὃς λαλεῖ βλασφημίας; τίς δύναται ⸂ἁμαρτίας ἀφεῖναι⸃ εἰ μὴ μόνος ὁ θεός;

verses.restored: Jesus, knowing their reasonings, answered them, Why are you reasoning in your hearts?

familiar.text: But when Jesus perceived their thoughts, he answering said unto them, What reason ye in your hearts?

modern.text: Knowing what they were thinking, Jesus replied, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?

original.text: ἐπιγνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν;

verses.restored: Which is easier: to say, Your sins/misalignments are released for you, or to say, Rise and walk?

familiar.text: Whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Rise up and walk?

modern.text: Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk?’

original.text: τί ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν· Ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου, ἢ εἰπεῖν· ⸀Ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει;

verses.restored: But so that you may know that the Son of Humanity has authority on earth to release sins/misalignments, he said to the paralyzed one, I say to you, rise, take up your bed, and go to your house.

familiar.text: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power upon earth to forgive sins, (he said unto the sick of the palsy,) I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy couch, and go into thine house.

modern.text: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins...” He said to the paralytic, “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”

original.text: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ⸂ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐξουσίαν ἔχει⸃ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας— εἶπεν τῷ παραλελυμένῳ· Σοὶ λέγω, ⸀ἔγειρε καὶ ἄρας τὸ κλινίδιόν σου πορεύου εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.

verses.restored: Immediately rising before them, he took up what he had been lying on and went to his house, glorifying the Divine.

familiar.text: And immediately he rose up before them, and took up that whereon he lay, and departed to his own house, glorifying God.

modern.text: And immediately the man stood up before them, took what he had been lying on, and went home glorifying God.

original.text: καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀναστὰς ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν, ἄρας ἐφʼ ὃ κατέκειτο, ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ δοξάζων τὸν θεόν.

verses.restored: Astonishment seized them all; they glorified the Divine and were filled with fear, saying, We have seen remarkable things today.

familiar.text: And they were all amazed, and they glorified God, and were filled with fear, saying, We have seen strange things to day.

modern.text: Everyone was taken with amazement and glorified God. They were filled with awe and said, “We have seen remarkable things today.” Jesus Calls Levi (Matthew 9:9–13; Mark 2:13–17)

original.text: καὶ ἔκστασις ἔλαβεν ἅπαντας καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεόν, καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν φόβου λέγοντες ὅτι Εἴδομεν παράδοξα σήμερον.

verses.restored: After these things he went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth, and he said to him, Follow me.

familiar.text: And after these things he went forth, and saw a publican, named Levi, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he said unto him, Follow me.

modern.text: After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him,

original.text: Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξῆλθεν καὶ ἐθεάσατο τελώνην ὀνόματι Λευὶν καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι.

verses.restored: Leaving everything, he rose and followed him.

familiar.text: And he left all, rose up, and followed him.

modern.text: and Levi got up, left everything, and followed Him.

original.text: καὶ καταλιπὼν ⸀πάντα ἀναστὰς ⸀ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: Levi made a great feast for him in his house, and there was a great crowd of tax collectors and others reclining with them.

familiar.text: And Levi made him a great feast in his own house: and there was a great company of publicans and of others that sat down with them.

modern.text: Then Levi hosted a great banquet for Jesus at his house. A large crowd of tax collectors was there, along with others who were eating with them.

original.text: Καὶ ἐποίησεν δοχὴν μεγάλην Λευὶς αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἦν ὄχλος ⸂πολὺς τελωνῶν⸃ καὶ ἄλλων οἳ ἦσαν μετʼ αὐτῶν κατακείμενοι.

verses.restored: The Pharisees and their scribes were grumbling to his disciples, saying, Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners/misaligned ones?

familiar.text: But their scribes and Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, Why do ye eat and drink with publicans and sinners?

modern.text: But the Pharisees and their scribes complained to Jesus’ disciples, “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”

original.text: καὶ ἐγόγγυζον οἱ ⸂Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν⸃ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Διὰ τί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίετε καὶ πίνετε;

verses.restored: Jesus answered them, Those who are healthy do not need a physician, but those having harm.

familiar.text: And Jesus answering said unto them, They that are whole need not a physician; but they that are sick.

modern.text: Jesus answered, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.

original.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ὑγιαίνοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλὰ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες·

verses.restored: I have not come to call righteous ones but sinners/misaligned ones into turning/realignment.

familiar.text: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

modern.text: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.” Questions about Fasting (Matthew 9:14–15; Mark 2:18–20)

original.text: οὐκ ἐλήλυθα καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν.

verses.restored: They said to him, John's disciples fast often and make prayers, likewise also those of the Pharisees, but yours eat and drink.

familiar.text: And they said unto him, Why do the disciples of John fast often, and make prayers, and likewise the disciples of the Pharisees; but thine eat and drink?

modern.text: Then they said to Him, “John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees frequently fast and pray, but Yours keep on eating and drinking.”

original.text: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν· ⸀Οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου νηστεύουσιν πυκνὰ καὶ δεήσεις ποιοῦνται, ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ τῶν Φαρισαίων, οἱ δὲ σοὶ ἐσθίουσιν καὶ πίνουσιν.

verses.restored: Jesus said to them, Can you make the sons of the bridal chamber fast while the bridegroom is with them?

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Can ye make the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them?

modern.text: Jesus replied, “Can you make the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them?

original.text: ὁ ⸀δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Μὴ δύνασθε τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ νυμφῶνος ἐν ᾧ ὁ νυμφίος μετʼ αὐτῶν ἐστιν ποιῆσαι ⸀νηστεῦσαι;

verses.restored: Days will come, and when the bridegroom is taken away from them, then they will fast in those days.

familiar.text: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.

modern.text: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.” The Patches and the Wineskins (Matthew 9:16–17; Mark 2:21–22)

original.text: ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι, καὶ ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος τότε νηστεύσουσιν ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις.

verses.restored: He also spoke a parable to them: No one tears a patch from a new garment and puts it on an old garment; otherwise the new will be torn, and the patch from the new will not match the old.

familiar.text: And he spake also a parable unto them; No man putteth a piece of a new garment upon an old; if otherwise, then both the new maketh a rent, and the piece that was taken out of the new agreeth not with the old.

modern.text: He also told them a parable: “No one tears a piece of cloth from a new garment and sews it on an old one. If he does, he will tear the new garment as well, and the patch from the new will not match the old.

original.text: ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Οὐδεὶς ἐπίβλημα ⸀ἀπὸ ἱματίου καινοῦ ⸀σχίσας ἐπιβάλλει ἐπὶ ἱμάτιον παλαιόν· εἰ δὲ μήγε, καὶ τὸ καινὸν ⸀σχίσει καὶ τῷ παλαιῷ οὐ ⸂συμφωνήσει τὸ ἐπίβλημα⸃ τὸ ἀπὸ τοῦ καινοῦ.

verses.restored: No one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the new wine will burst the skins, and it will be spilled, and the skins destroyed.

familiar.text: And no man putteth new wine into old bottles; else the new wine will burst the bottles, and be spilled, and the bottles shall perish.

modern.text: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the new wine will burst the skins, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined.

original.text: καὶ οὐδεὶς βάλλει οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς· εἰ δὲ μήγε, ῥήξει ὁ ⸂οἶνος ὁ νέος⸃ τοὺς ἀσκούς, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐκχυθήσεται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοὶ ἀπολοῦνται·

verses.restored: But new wine must be put into fresh wineskins.

familiar.text: But new wine must be put into new bottles; and both are preserved.

modern.text: Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.

original.text: ἀλλὰ οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινοὺς ⸀βλητέον.

verses.restored: And no one drinking old wine desires new, for he says, The old is good/useful.

familiar.text: No man also having drunk old wine straightway desireth new: for he saith, The old is better.

modern.text: And no one after drinking old wine wants new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’”

original.text: ⸀καὶ οὐδεὶς πιὼν ⸀παλαιὸν θέλει νέον· λέγει γάρ· Ὁ παλαιὸς ⸀χρηστός ἐστιν.
